newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed on light volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed on light volumes.

text.p: New York precious metals ended mixed Tuesday, wity light volumes light for the second day in a row, as the complex continued to consolidate after seeing multi-month lows last week.

"Support in December gold is now drawn at $374 and beyond that at $370," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said. "Above the market there is thin line of resistance at $380, the next major stop is at $384-385."
"Open interest in this market remains high and the expiration of the December gold options contracts on Friday could lend some upward pressure on prices," he said.
COMEX December gold ended unchanged at $379.60 an ounce, after trading in a $379.40-380.50 range on light estimated total volume of 18,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $378.50/379.00, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $379.25 and the New York close Monday at $378.60/379.00.
COMEX December silver ended down 1.5 cents at $4.793 an ounce, after seeing a $4.780-4.830 range on estimated total volume of just 7,000 lots.
"As long as prices continue to fall, investors will not be buying silver," Kempf said.
"Movements in precious metals markets remain purely technical in nature and there are no changes in the foreseeable future that are likely to attract investors back to these markets," he said.

Precious metals had discounted a win by President Clinton in the U.S. election Tuesday, and apparently successful heart surgery on Russian president Yeltsin overnight Monday reduced the risk of political instability, reducing the incentive for investors to buy gold, traders said.

A fresh fall in U.S. bond yields Tuesday to six month lows, after U.S. September house completions fell 5.8 pct, also meant there was no inflationary threat, and little need for gold as an inflation hedge, analysts said.
Open interest in COMEX gold futures stood at 192,687 lots on November 1, after rising in the past 10 days as spot gold prices slipped to its lowest levels since March 1995 last week.

In the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report, for the week ended October 22, large non-commercial traders held a record net short position of 36,015 lots in COMEX gold futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Open interest in COMEX silver futures stood at 97,204 lots on November 1.

But open interest in the December silver contract alone stood at 63,295 lots, representing 316 million ounces of silver, compared with COMEX silver warehouse stocks which stand near 10 year lows at only 132 million Tuesday.
NYMEX January platinum ended down $1.10 an ounce Tuesday at $384.00, while NYMEX December palladium closed 35 cents at $118.00.
The April 1997 platinum/gold spread has recovered from zero again in the past 10 days to end at $2.3 an ounce Tuesday.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
